title: Paddle pickup procedure through the robot API (paddle-success-v1 owner profile)
evidence: One observed success on 2026-10-07 (see physical_pickup_handoff and the repo README software/docs/commissioning/2026-10-07-paddle-success/README.md). Station-specific; not a keyframe replay and not a repeatability claim.
not_yet_physically_validated: Several joints moving together in one command
Bounded settle corrections and the settled_short outcome
owner_preconditions: robot_get_execution shows execution_profile paddle-success-v1, phase idle or holding, ok true, status age under 1 s (stop_latched is always false: there is no STOP latch). After a STOP or fault the owner is already back to idle with every motor released; no restart is needed, enable explicitly. Only a wrong profile or a missing or stale owner needs a restart on the robot Mac with ./restart-robot-server.sh (motors released first).
Owner scope is the six right-arm joints only; left arm and head are read-only; the wheels are driven only through robot_move_base pulses (owner started with --wheels).

Phone side view fresh: work/phone_camera/latest.json received_at under 10 s old with a seq. Enable and every new target are refused otherwise. While holding, a stale feed pauses target advancement; after 20 s stale the owner releases torque and a held paddle drops.
Every right-arm joint at least 40 ticks inside its saved range when enabling; a folded rest pose near a limit is refused.
Supply voltage raw 100..140 on all six joints.
enable: robot_set_motor_enable with all six right-arm names and enabled=true in one call. Every motion command is refused until all six are enabled. Torque ceilings 800 (elbow 400, gripper 500), speed 100 (gripper 200), acceleration 5, shoulder-lift and elbow P 32; originals restore on release.
hold_lease: Enable and each finished move (including settled_short) grant a 120 s monitored hold. Re-sending robot_set_motor_enable for the same six joints while holding renews it to 120 s (camera must be fresh). When it expires the owner releases torque and a held paddle drops.

motion_rules.per_joint_segment_ticks: 3..341 from the measured position; targets and goals stay 40 ticks inside saved ranges
motion_rules.simultaneous: One robot_move_joint_targets call may move several right-arm joints; they ramp together in 40-tick steps (no faster than every 0.4 s) and arrive on the same step. Moves over 341 ticks are split into <=280-tick segments.
motion_rules.gripper_closing: A closing gripper is always run alone, after the other joints of the same call. It advances 10 ticks per step, waits 0.3 s stationary, max 1.5 s per step, and stops when stationary closing error reaches 40 ticks: closure_outcome stationary_closure_unverified, grasp_verified false.
motion_rules.following_envelope: Each joint must stay within 96 ticks of its commanded goal or the owner faults and releases all motors; the move is cancelled and motors stay released until an explicit robot_set_motor_enable.
motion_rules.segment_budget: 20 motion segments per owner session (settled_short moves count). A STOP does not reset it; only an owner restart does, and a restart needs the arm released, so never run out while holding the paddle.

settling.endpoint_settled: Three fresh samples with velocity below 3, sample change at most 3, Moving flag 0, and endpoint error at most 57 ticks (gripper 30).
settling.corrections: If a joint comes to rest short of target (gravity sag), the owner overdrives its held goal by the measured residual: at most 40 ticks per write, at most 57 ticks beyond target, never more than 90 ticks from the present position, at most 3 corrections, within an extra 5 s.
settling.settled_short: If a joint is still short at rest after corrections, the move returns completed=false, endpoint_reached=false, closure_outcome=settled_short, settle_residual_ticks per joint, motors holding (no STOP). Re-plan from the readbacks or call robot_stop.
settling.deadline_fault: A joint that never comes to rest by the deadline still faults: all motors released and the move cancelled, never resumed. There is no latch: the owner returns to idle and motors stay released until an explicit robot_set_motor_enable.

observed_start_pose_note: Pan, lift, elbow and gripper are measured starts from the table; wrist flex and roll are the held targets. Re-measure before every move.

observed_sequence.note: resistance stop, load 328; empty-jaw baseline endpoint 1331, load 176

sequence_note: Commands were relative to fresh measured positions. Each pilot step is one segment (13 total, budget 20). Steps 12 and 13 can be one simultaneous call. Use robot_set_gripper or a lower gripper target for CLOSE. Check cameras after every segment; locally correct a healthy held pose on an empty miss instead of resetting the arm.

cameras.phone: Side view of handle and both fingers; required by the owner (receipt time, not capture time).
cameras.oak: Head RGB/depth; raw distorted fallback unless a rectified stream declares itself.
cameras.right_wrist: Native wrist camera (AVFoundation 0x12200005a39230), request explicitly in robot_get_cameras. Used during the original success.
cameras.left_wrist: AVFoundation 0x12140005a39230; known to freeze, expect camera_errors until its cable is reseated.
cameras.calibration: No camera is calibrated to the robot frame; images guide the operator, they do not authorize motion.

success_criteria: Only call it a pickup when the paddle follows the jaws, visibly clears the table, stays held, and can be placed and released without a passive drop. Resistance, tool success, simulation or an image description alone are not a grasp.
stop_and_recovery: robot_stop releases all motors and cancels any move in progress; so does any owner fault. There is no STOP latch: the owner returns to phase idle and records last_stop (time, reason, command_id, released, release_errors) and stop_count. A cancelled move is never resumed and nothing re-enables by itself: motors stay released until an explicit robot_set_motor_enable, which repeats every health, range, camera and voltage check. Recovery needs no owner restart: read last_stop, fresh state, readiness and cameras, deal with the cause of the fault, enable all six joints explicitly, and re-plan from fresh readbacks. If readiness shows OWNER_NOT_HEALTHY, a torque-off release failed: that is a hardware problem; call robot_stop again and do not enable until it confirms the release. ./restart-robot-server.sh is for deploying new code, not for clearing a STOP. Never replay requests from an earlier owner session.
do_not: Call robot_get_registered_tags as a prerequisite; tag registration is not part of this procedure.
Replay the sequence blindly after power-off, manual arm movement or cart repositioning.
Use Cartesian reach/FK proposals as motor targets.
Drive the base while an arm move runs (refused), or chain base pulses without checking cameras between them.

base_drive.limits: Each wheel at most 0.02 m/s (straight |linear_m_s|<=0.02, in-place |angular_rad_s|<=0.16, positive turns left); duration at most 3 s per call (about 6 cm).
base_drive.behavior: Both wheels switch to velocity mode for the pulse, then brake, settle, release torque and restore settings. They are never left powered. A stale phone feed brakes early. Wheel status, load<=500, velocity<=400 and 10-14 V are checked every sample. Any failure or robot_stop stops the wheels and releases all motors.
base_drive.arm: Allowed with the arm released or holding; refused while an arm move runs. The original 5.43 cm approach used three 1 s pulses with the arm released.
base_drive.result: Wheel encoder deltas and an estimated travel in cm; slip and actual cart travel are unverified, so check cameras after each pulse.
base_drive.validation: Ported from the hardware-validated drive-pulse.py; not yet run through the API.
